newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Generali 's Providencia sees '97 profit up.
newsitem.headline: Generali 's Providencia sees '97 profit up.

text.p: Hungarian insurer Providencia Rt, majority-owned by Austria's EA-Generali AG said on Thursday it expected its 1997 profit to exceed last year's profit by 30 percent.
"We expect an almost 30 percent increase in premium revenues for 1997 and a similar increase of profits," Mihaly Palvolgyi, Providencia general manager, told a news conference.
Another company official said 1996 was the third consecutive year when the company posted a profit but due to rollover losses this was the first year of actual profit to shareholders.
"Our 1996 net profit was 465 million forints, and after deducting losses of previous years some 100 million remains," said Deputy General Manager Karoly Gergely.
He added that according to the decision of a general meeting held two weeks ago, the amount would be retained to increase the insurance company's reserves.
Gergely said Providencia had premium revenues of 17.7 billion forints last year, an increase of 31 percent over 1995.
Providencia, despite harsh competition from Nationale Nederlanden 's Hungarian unit, managed to maintain its third position in the market and aims at keeping it in the future.
"The two formerly state-owned insurance companies still have such an advantage that it would be unrealistic to aim for second place," Palvolgyi said.
Hungary's total 1996 premium revenues are estimated at 150 billion forints.

The market leader, Hungaria Biztosito Rt, wholly owned by Germany's Allianz AG, reported premium revenues of 49.2 billion forints for 1996. The second biggest insurer, AB-Aegon, wholly owned by Dutch Aegon International BV said its 1996 premuim revenue was 35.5 billion forints.
